title: Arkret Device Key Operation DTOs
description: Closed request and response DTOs for ak.keys.{upload,query,claim}, the Station-to-Station device directory read and ak.keys.backups.{put,list,delete}. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.

request_id.description: Client-generated idempotency id. The service keys the canonical request digest and terminal outcome by (account_id, backup_id, request_id).

keys_backups_delete_proof.description: High-risk authority proof over the canonical delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1. Exactly one of recovery_unlock, device_quorum or trusted_recovery_service; an ordinary current-device session proof is not accepted for active-series tail deletion.

account_device_key_entries.description: One entry per exact AccountId. Entries MUST be sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes of RFC 8785 JCS(account_id); duplicate AccountIds MUST be rejected even when values differ.

did_key.description: Authoritative device signing key as an Ed25519 did:key (multibase base58btc, multicodec ed25519-pub). Mirrors ak.device.authorize.payload.device_public_key_did (device-lifecycle.md §5.2 / §5.4). To check SignalEnvelope and durable Event proofs, receivers resolve a verification_method DID URL under the verified principal did, validate its bare did through the registered adapter, require project(did) to equal the actor/principal did_core_id, and require its fragment to equal the full ak:device:<uuidv7> id. Constructing a verification method by appending a fragment to did_core_id is forbidden.

device_generation_state.description: Reducer-managed identity-root generation fence for the principal device directory.

current_device_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic generation; it is not and MUST NOT be derived from a DID versionId.

account_device_generation_entries.description: Current device-generation fence for each exact AccountId. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

device_projection_attestation_core.description: Origin Station assertion that this exact device projection is the account's current accepted one. It is the whole verification closure of the Station-to-Station device directory read and of the account_device signer evidence: the attested body carries no PCR genesis receipt, no device authorization chain and no accepted RealmCommit, because that material is account-internal governance and is disclosed only through ak.self.identity.read.resolution_audit.v1 under exact current-holder authorization. Required device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref fields describe the closed shape of a returned usable row; they do not require an unauthorized device to have a partial projection. A device with no current accepted authorization is omitted or reported through the non-enumerating failure shape. attested_at is a monotone freshness marker and, with authorized_generation_ref, is the cache key of device-lifecycle.md section 8.3.

account_id.description: Exact account owning the device projection. The proof controller MUST project exactly onto account_id.station_id; an attestation that verifies under any other Station key is not evidence about this account.

device_status.description: This surface attests usable devices only. A revoked or fenced device is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so the attested status is constant rather than a disclosure channel.

attested_at.description: MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at and MUST equal proof.created_at.

expires_at.description: Fresh current-query cache deadline only. Expiry does not revoke the signed device authorization or prohibit ordinary publication with verified cached evidence. Security operations use their stricter registered current-state gate.

authorization_window.description: Exact source device authorization window. null expiry means no time limit. This is distinct from attestation cache freshness; ordinary publication uses this window and applicable revocation closures.

device_projection_attestation.description: Complete origin-Station-signed device projection attestation. The detached proof signs the ak.device_projection_attestation_proof.v1 transcript; proof.created_at MUST equal attestation.attested_at.

verified_device_projection.description: The device projection a client receives from its own authenticated Station on the self keys/query surface. The values are the ones the Station read out of the origin Station's verified device_projection_attestation; the row therefore carries no origin proof and no wrapper whose only job was to verify that proof, and a client MUST NOT treat this projection as portable evidence about the origin. account_id and device_id are not repeated here: they are the enclosing entry's account_id and the device_keys map key, and the returning Station MUST have checked that the verified attestation named exactly that pair before projecting it. attested_at is the origin's own observation instant, forwarded verbatim; together with authorized_generation_ref it is the cache key of device-lifecycle.md section 8.3. Required device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref describe the closed shape of a usable row; a device with no current accepted authorization is omitted or reported through the non-enumerating failure shape rather than degraded into a partial projection.

device_status.description: This surface projects usable devices only. A revoked or fenced device is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so the projected status is constant rather than a disclosure channel.

attested_at.description: Origin observation instant of the verified projection, forwarded verbatim. MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at.

expires_at.description: Fresh current-query cache deadline only, forwarded verbatim from the verified origin attestation. The returning Station MUST NOT extend it. Expiry does not revoke the signed device authorization or prohibit ordinary publication with verified cached evidence.

authorization_window.description: Exact source device authorization window, forwarded verbatim. null expiry means no time limit. This is distinct from cache freshness; ordinary publication uses this window and applicable revocation closures.

query_device_record.description: Per-(account_id, device_id) entry in keys_query_outcome, the client-facing self surface. account_id and device_id are the device_keys entry and map keys, not row fields. The row is the restricted typed result the client's own authenticated Station produces after it verified the origin Station's device_projection_attestation, so it carries the verified projection plus the prekey material and the signer_evidence_ref the client actually uses, and never the origin proof or its verification wrapper. A device whose generation is fenced, or which is revoked, is not degraded into a partial row -- it is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so an incomplete row can never be mistaken for a usable one.

signer_evidence_ref.description: Exact account_device signer evidence the origin Station retained with its Station attester closure before the row was returned. It keeps pointing at that complete immutable evidence object: it is neither recomputed from this pruned projection nor an additional device-authority claim.

trust_algorithms.description: The canonical (UTF-8 bytewise sorted, deduplicated) algorithm ids echoed verbatim from ak.device.authorize.payload.algorithms; together with device_signing_key and hpke_key this is the material the section 5.2 ak.device-trust-bind-v1 transcript covers. Distinct from the sibling `algorithms` prekey-bundle map.

query_account_device_entries.description: One device-key result group per exact AccountId on the self surface. The returning Station MUST have matched each verified attestation's account_id and device_id against this account_id and its enclosing device_id key before projecting the row. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

peer_query_device_record.description: Per-(account_id, device_id) entry in peer_keys_query_outcome, the Station-to-Station surface. account_id and device_id are the device_keys entry and map keys, not row fields. Every returned row is complete and attested: the origin Station signs the exact projection, so the requesting Station can verify the row without ever seeing PCR material. This is deliberately a different type from the client-facing query_device_record: the signed attestation is the object the requesting Station verifies, and a Station MUST NOT turn an unverified peer row into a client result by dropping its proof. A device whose generation is fenced, or which is revoked, is not degraded into a partial row -- it is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so an incomplete row can never be mistaken for a usable one.

signer_evidence_ref.description: Exact account_device signer evidence retained with its Station attester closure before this row is returned. Its embedded attestation equals this row's attestation byte for byte; the ref is not an additional device-authority claim.

trust_algorithms.description: The canonical (UTF-8 bytewise sorted, deduplicated) algorithm ids echoed verbatim from ak.device.authorize.payload.algorithms; together with device_signing_key and hpke_key this is the material the §5.2 ak.device-trust-bind-v1 transcript covers. Distinct from the sibling `algorithms` prekey-bundle map.

device_projection_attestation.description: Origin-Station signature over the authoritative device projection. Consumers read device_signing_key_did, hpke_key, device_status, device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref from the verified attestation. Its account_id and device_id MUST match the enclosing result group and device key; its signer MUST project onto account_id.station_id.

peer_query_account_device_entries.description: One device-key result group per exact AccountId on the Station-to-Station surface. Each signed device projection MUST match this account_id and its enclosing device_id key. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

account_device_algorithm_entries.description: One claim target group per exact AccountId. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

query_account_device_selectors.description: Explicit account/device selectors sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes of RFC 8785 JCS(account_id). Neither AccountId component may be inferred from the target service, caller session or another entry. Duplicate AccountIds MUST be rejected; use one entry containing all selected device_ids for that account. At most 16 accounts and 32 devices per account bound the local read and its cross-Station fan-out alike; an over-limit request fails whole and is never truncated.

query_failure.description: Closed non-enumerating failure row for the device directory read surfaces. device_result_unavailable covers absent, invisible, unrelated, revoked, fenced and policy-denied targets with one indistinguishable value. device_directory_unavailable states only that the requester's own Station could not obtain or verify a current attested projection this time; it never depends on target state and MUST NOT be rendered as an omitted row or an empty device set.

retry_after_ms.description: Only meaningful with device_directory_unavailable; a target-private failure MUST NOT carry it.

encryption.description: Non-secret recipient metadata so the client can categorize a backup (recovery_public_key vs passphrase_kdf vs secret_storage_key) without downloading the ciphertext. The aead/kdf material is withheld from the list summary.

device_generations.description: Current identity-root generation fence by exact AccountId. Fenced accounts or mismatched device generations expose no usable signing/HPKE/prekey material.

peer_keys_query_purpose.description: Declared use of the requested directory rows. The destination authorizes each purpose independently and MUST NOT clear the broadest one once.

peer_keys_relationship_basis.description: Closed relationship the requester asserts. The destination re-derives it from its own accepted state; a caller assertion never authorizes by itself. The contact branch deliberately carries no realm_id: a legitimate Contact needs no shared Realm.

peer_keys_query_request_body.description: Station-to-Station device directory and published prekey-bundle read. It is the only registered carrier for a cross-Station keys/query target: the client asks its own Station, which authenticates itself with its own RFC 9421 service signature and never forwards a client SessionGrant, DPoP or any local bearer. Single authority, single hop, read only. Cross-Station single-use material stays with the MLS KeyPackage claim contract.

request_id.description: Stable typed id the requesting Station mints for this fetch. The destination uses it only for correlation and rate limiting and keeps no durable ledger.

requester_account_id.description: Exact requesting account. Its station_id MUST equal the authenticated Source-Service-ID and MUST NOT be inferred from a principal component, route or session.

device_keys.description: Targets for this destination only: every account_id.station_id MUST equal the authenticated Destination-Service-ID.

peer_keys_query_outcome.description: Verbatim origin-signed rows plus the closed non-enumerating failure shape. The destination does not add a response signature layer: every row carries the origin's own device_projection_attestation and signer_evidence_ref, and the requesting Station MUST verify them before projecting the restricted client-facing query_device_record.

keys_backups_list.description: Bounded Account Station metadata page with the current accepted secret_storage backup-class pointer, independent of list filters. key-management.md section 7.6.1 fixes cursor and unknown-state semantics.

keys_backups_unlock_request_body.description: Closed exact single-object unlock intent. Branch authority, current validity, exact account/device/object, challenge and signature must all verify before durable allowance/budget/result commit. An identical retry by the same still-authorized holder returns the stored object without double charge.

keys_backups_issue_delete_challenge_requ.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.command.issue_delete_challenge.v1. While an issued challenge for the same (account_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid, the service MUST return the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new challenge.

keys_backups_delete_challenge.description: Server-issued, durable, single-use delete challenge (TTL <= 300s). Every field is materialized by the service; the client echoes challenge_id in the DELETE body and every proof signs the canonical delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1, which embeds these exact values. Replay, expiry, path mismatch, or audience/service mismatch MUST fail closed.

challenge_id.description: Server-issued unique id of this challenge; echoed verbatim in the DELETE request body.

challenge.description: Server-issued CSPRNG challenge bytes (base64url, no padding).

nonce.description: Server-issued CSPRNG nonce bytes (base64url, no padding); distinct from challenge so the transcript binds two independent freshness values.

account_id.description: Exact account that owns the backup and challenge; both principal and Station components are signed by every delete proof.

audience.description: The service base origin this challenge is valid against; MUST match the origin the DELETE request is sent to.

request_id.description: Echo of the issuance request_id this challenge was minted for.

keys_backups_delete_request_body.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.resource.delete.v1. The service verifies the referenced challenge against the current caller/path/service, verifies the high-risk proof over the canonical delete-intent transcript, and consumes the challenge in the same transaction as the successful delete. A byte-identical network retry returns the stored terminal outcome without re-admitting the consumed challenge; the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

challenge_id.description: Exact echo of the server-issued challenge_id being consumed.

keys_backups_issue_unlock_challenge_requ.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.command.issue_unlock_challenge.v1. While an issued challenge for the same (account_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid, the service MUST return the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new challenge.

keys_backups_unlock_challenge.description: Shared-durable single-use current-device unlock challenge, TTL <= 300 seconds, scoped to authenticated account/device, exact backup/series/ciphertext, origin and service. All values are server materialized. Recovery-session unlock reuses its session challenge and MUST NOT call this operation.

challenge.description: Server-issued CSPRNG challenge bytes (base64url, no padding).

nonce.description: Server-issued CSPRNG nonce bytes (base64url, no padding); distinct from challenge so the transcript binds two independent freshness values.

request_id.description: Echo of the issuance request_id this challenge was minted for.
